findings.requirement: The merge is the one hold on unapproved or conflicting intent
findings.what: Check 1: the statement says the push is 'the one full run' and example 24 says the pre-push hook is 'the one full test run' (the intent's wont says the same: 'the one full run is at push'). Read plainly, every push runs the whole suite. That contradicts INT-027, the very record this file quotes: its confirmed wont is 'Run the full suite routinely' and its will is 'a full run only for a named reason (for example a change to shared test infrastructure)'. It also contradicts the P10 draft, where the full suite runs only for a named reason, at most once per merge check, and the owner can waive it through the question tool. The old wording (SR-051, SR-077/EX-8, and SR-083/EX-5 which P14 supersedes) predates the P10 answer. Say instead that the pre-push hook runs the merge check with its covering tests, and the full suite only when full verification is pending (P10), and reword example 24 and the intent's wont to match.

findings.requirement: The merge is the one hold on unapproved or conflicting intent
findings.what: Check 3: several behaviours in one. The 31 examples cover (a) the hold set (approval, extension by link or exemption, undeclared paths, stale links, conflicts, exit-code precedence), (b) the commit-msg trailer check at commit time (examples 8, 18, 19 are not merge-time at all), (c) hook installation and foreign hooks left alone (3, 22, 24), (d) the report cap and the report-only form (2, 11), (e) rebase, cherry-pick and revert steps (28), (f) finishing a merge by hand (27) and (g) the fast-forward put-back (31). Split at least the commit-time trailer check and the hook installation from the hold; a reader of the statement cannot tell they exist.

findings.requirement: The merge is the one hold on unapproved or conflicting intent
findings.what: Check 4: statement and examples disagree. The statement never mentions a failing or unverified acceptance test, exit 5 or the exit-code precedence, yet example 7 asserts 'exits 5 (precedence 1, then 5, then 4)' (from SR-049). P10 owns the exit-5 rule, but nothing says the precedence belongs here or there; state it once. The statement also says a rebase step is held 'until every touched requirement is approved', while the only rebase example (28) and the source SR-077 hold a rebase, cherry-pick or revert step on an open intent conflict alone; and the statement names merge, rebase and cherry-pick while example 28 adds revert.

findings.requirement: Record files merge field by field, and a same-field clash becomes one intent conflict
findings.what: Check 4 and 3: the statement stops at 'shows it once ... until it is settled', but 7 of the 13 examples assert other behaviours it never states: how the conflict is put to the owner (9, 12), how the answer is recorded and the record reconfirmed (10), that the agent cannot settle it (11), example-number collisions (3) and the driver being declared once (4). Fold these into the statement or split the settling of a conflict out. It also overlaps the P3 requirement 'The owner arbitrates a conflict through a question' (agent refused, question-tool answer chosen), so the same behaviour is asserted in two requirements; keep it in one.

findings.requirement: Intent in flight is shared, and a contradicting capture is caught before any build
findings.what: Check 3 and 4: two behaviours in one (the claims register and the awareness lines, versus the capture-time contradiction question with its early decision). The statement says nothing about the under-50-ms read-only scan (examples 1 to 4), the early decision that outlives the question (18, 19, 21), the 'differs from the owner's answer every turn' signal (22, 23) or 'changed on main after this branch started' (24), though all are asserted. List them in the statement or split the early-conflict half into its own requirement.

findings.requirement: Record files merge field by field, and a same-field clash becomes one intent conflict
findings.what: Check 5: the proof plan cannot show what it promises. It has one branch add 'a link and an example' and the other 'a link and a different statement': only one side changes the statement, so there is no same-field clash and the owner would see a silent merge and no question. Make both branches change the statement differently (and optionally have one also add a link and an example, to show the rest merging on its own).

findings.requirement: Intent in flight is shared, and a contradicting capture is caught before any build
findings.what: Check 4: example 20 has a double given ('no judge can be reached, or JEV is unsure') and a then-clause ending 'no word rule judges in its place', which nobody can watch. Split it into the unreachable-judge case ('judging unavailable: <cause>' reaches the agent) and the unsure case (the two versions are put to the owner if they differ); drop the negative clause or make it observable (a differing overlap is never reported as compatible). The tension with P8 (no judge reachable: plumb holds the step) should also be said once.

findings.requirement: Intent in flight is shared, and a contradicting capture is caught before any build

SR-081/EX-11 has no draft example of its own (its trigger paths are folded into 15 and 16 and its 'answered before anything is written' part is a card behaviour that goes with P12). SR-081/EX-10 loses 'keep this one' or 'theirs' being refused on main and a branch's name recording exactly that version, and SR-081/EX-12 loses the refused ok. P2 and P3 justify the ok parts, but the 'keep this one' refusal is a behaviour with linked tests (SR-081 has 15) that is neither carried nor listed as dropped.

findings.requirement: Record ids never collide across worktrees and clones
findings.what: Check 3: three mechanisms in one requirement (reservation through the shared ref, merge-fix renumbering, and the merge check holding a collision), and the hold in examples 12 to 14 is also in the R4 statement ('no ids collide'), so the same behaviour is stated twice. Keep reservation and renumbering here and leave the hold to the merge requirement, or the reverse. Example 11 shows the owner a label 'carried by renumber SR-070 -> SR-081'; P2 says the owner never needs record ids, so say it is shown to the agent in the merge report, or word it by title (check 8, kept low because no command or card is involved).

findings.what: Wording and bookkeeping: 'decides' lists DEC-020 and DEC-021, which the file's own decisions supersede, and DEC-021 is also in R4's decides; the new decisions flip 'matters' from false (DEC-020, DEC-021, DEC-022 in the dump) to true without a reason.
